title: Ghost Dance Guide — Ghost Shrouds, Evasion-based ES Regeneration and Spirit
summary: Ghost Dance is a Spirit gem that grants Ghost Shrouds. When you take a hit that does not completely avoid damage, you consume a Shroud and recover Energy Shield equal to a portion of your Evasion. The 0.5 version was reworked, so old 'instant recover on shroud loss' advice no longer applies. This guide covers Shroud stacking, hit rules, Evasion-to-ES recovery, Spirit cost and synergy with Wind Dancer.
description: Ghost Dance deep guide: Spirit cost, Ghost Shroud stacking and cadence, which hits consume a Shroud, Evasion-based Energy Shield recovery, Wind Dancer synergy, Spirit budget vs Herald, mapping and boss value, troubleshooting and community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: In 0.5, Ghost Dance grants Ghost Shrouds; when you take a non-fully-avoided hit, a Shroud is consumed and you recover Energy Shield based on your Evasion.
It is not the old 'instant full recover on shroud loss' — the recovery is tied to Evasion and the current hit, so the old guides are outdated.
You need both Evasion and some Energy Shield for it to matter; pure-Life or pure-ES-low-Evasion characters get little value.

sections.title: Version Warning (0.5 Rework)
paragraphs: The 0.5 Ghost Dance was reworked. The old description — consume a Ghost Shroud and immediately recover Energy Shield equal to a percentage of Evasion — does not directly map to the current version.
Treat any pre-0.5 'instant recover' advice as outdated. Verify the current recovery rule on the in-game tooltip before building around it.
bullets: Old instant-recover behaviour is not the current rule.
Confirm the recovery formula on the live tooltip.
Evasion still drives the recovery amount.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Ghost Dance reserves 30 Spirit, so you need spare Spirit after Herald or other spirit skills. It needs Evasion and at least some Energy Shield to provide value.

sections.title: Persistent Buff
paragraphs: While reserved, Ghost Dance passively grants and refreshes Ghost Shrouds on a timer up to the cap. The buff is always on; you do not activate it per hit.
bullets: Shrouds fill on a cadence up to the cap.
Buff is passive while Spirit is reserved.
Cooldown recovery rate changes the refill frequency.

sections.title: Ghost Shrouds
paragraphs: Ghost Shrouds are charges that absorb a hit. When you take a hit that is not fully evaded or otherwise avoided, one Shroud is consumed.
Evaded hits, and hits fully avoided by block or deflect, do not consume a Shroud because no damage was taken. Damage over Time also does not consume a Shroud in the same way as a discrete hit.
After a Shroud is consumed, the current version recovers Energy Shield based on your Evasion rather than granting an instant full recover.
bullets: A non-avoided hit consumes one Shroud.
Evaded / blocked / deflected hits do not consume.
Recovery is Evasion-based, not instant full.

sections.title: Hit Behaviour
paragraphs: Each discrete hit that deals damage can consume a Shroud. Multiple hits in quick succession consume multiple Shrouds, which is why a high-frequency boss can strip your Shrouds fast.
Whether a hit 'recently' consumed a Shroud and refreshed recovery depends on the current client rule; do not assume every hit stacks recovery.
bullets: Each damaging hit can take a Shroud.
Bosses with many small hits drain Shrouds quickly.
Evaded and fully avoided hits are free.

sections.title: Evasion and Energy Shield Analysis
paragraphs: Ghost Dance scales with Evasion: higher Evasion means more Energy Shield recovered per Shroud. But you also need an Energy Shield pool for the recovery to land in.
A high-Evasion, high-ES character gets the most value. High-Evasion low-ES may overflow recovery; low-Evasion high-ES recovers little; pure-Life has no ES to recover into.
bullets: More Evasion: more ES recovered per Shroud.
Need an ES pool to receive the recovery.
Pure-Life gets little value.

sections.title: Spirit Budget
paragraphs: Ghost Dance costs 30 Spirit. Against a Herald that also wants Spirit, you must choose: the Herald adds offensive aura value, Ghost Dance adds defensive recovery.
Quality that improves reservation efficiency reduces the effective Spirit cost, freeing budget for both.
bullets: 30 Spirit reservation.
Competes with Herald for Spirit.
Quality reservation efficiency helps fit both.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: As a Spirit gem, Ghost Dance is slotted into a spirit socket; supports that affect spirit reservation or defense apply. Evasion and Energy Shield on your gear drive its value more than supports.
bullets: Reservation efficiency supports free Spirit.
Gear Evasion and ES matter most.
No direct damage supports.

sections.title: Mapping Value
paragraphs: In maps, you rarely start with full Shrouds; they fill as you fight. Ghost Dance helps survive map mods and porcupine rares by recovering ES between hits.
It is most valuable on Evasion characters that also invest in Energy Shield.
bullets: Shrouds fill during the map, not at entry.
Helps vs map damage spikes.
Best on Evasion + ES characters.

sections.title: Bossing Value
paragraphs: Against a boss with frequent hits, Ghost Dance recovers ES steadily but can be drained if the boss out-hits your Shroud refill. It is a smoothing layer, not a panic button.
Pair it with other recovery so a Shroud strip does not leave you exposed.
bullets: Steady ES recovery vs bosses.
High-frequency bosses can drain Shrouds.
Combine with other recovery.

sections.title: Build Usage
paragraphs: Ghost Dance fits Evasion-based characters that also run Energy Shield, such as Ice Shot Deadeye and Whirling Assault Martial Artist variants.
It synergises with Wind Dancer, which also rewards Evasion and dodging.
bullets: Ice Shot Deadeye: Evasion + ES recovery.
Whirling Assault Martial Artist: dodge-based defense.
Pairs with Wind Dancer.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: If you enter a map with no Shrouds, that is expected — they fill as you fight. If a boss strips them instantly, the boss out-hits your refill; add more Evasion or other recovery.
If recovery feels weak, your Evasion or Energy Shield is too low for the build.
bullets: No Shrouds at entry: expected, they fill.
Boss strips fast: out-hit by refill, add Evasion.
Weak recovery: raise Evasion and ES.
No ES pool: pure-Life gets little.
Spirit conflict: balance with Herald.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: After the 0.5 rework, community threads focus on the new Evasion-based recovery and warn that old Ghost Dance guides are wrong.
Players report it as a strong smoothing layer on Evasion characters that also invest in Energy Shield.
bullets: 0.5 rework changed the recovery rule.
Strong on Evasion + ES characters.
